# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – no standardised first-contact-to-first-class flow; risk of inconsistent experience and lost early retention signal
- **Member Checkins** – no cadence or framework for proactive engagement post-join; churn risk unmanaged
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no triggered intervention or win-back playbook; revenue leakage unquantified
- **Referral Programme** – no mechanics, incentives, or tracking; word-of-mouth left to chance
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – critical gap; legal and reputational risk, especially for women-only membership data
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no measurable standard for class delivery consistency; coach accountability vague

- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no progression framework; coach retention and capability building ad hoc

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with revenue reality, not perfection**
Don't overthink this. Pull your last 3 months of actual transactions—what are members *actually* buying? (Classes, PT sessions, nutrition plans, challenges?) List those first. Add 1-2 gaps you've noticed (members asking for things you don't offer). That's your menu. Done in an afternoon.

**2. Build two separate documents, not one**
- **Coach version**: What you deliver + time required + your profit margin per service. This stops vague "we'll figure it out" conversations.
- **Member version**: Clean, benefit-focused language. "4-week body composition plan: £49/month" not "nutritional coaching package." Price it so members say yes without friction.

**3. Price by testing, not guessing**
Pick your lowest-confidence service. Offer it to 5 members at your planned price this week. Listen for hesitation. If 3 push back, you know the number. If all 5 say yes immediately, you're underpriced. Move pricing after real data, not assumptions.

**4. Make coaches accountable to it immediately**
Share the coach version in your next team huddle. Ask each: "Which of these can you confidently sell and deliver this month?" Lock in commitments. A menu nobody sells is just a spreadsheet.

**5. Test it live before "launching"**
Post the member menu to your WhatsApp group or a quiet Instagram story this week. See what questions land. Adjust language based on actual confusion—then launch publicly.

**Goal: Functional menu in 2 weeks, not a polished one in 2

• **Rev/member has crashed to £106 in Aug (was £145 in July).** You've added 17 members (121→153) but revenue fell £3.6k. Root cause: new members on low-tier plans or discounted intro rates. Audit TeamUp pricing tiers; move new sign-ups to standard tier (currently underpriced vs £131–145 average). Target: £130+ rev/member by November.

• **May's 12.8% churn is your red flag.** Last 3 months (Jul–Sep) average 6.6% churn vs prior 3 (Feb–Apr) at 5.1%. Retention is drifting. Implement exit surveys in TeamUp; identify the May cohort and probe why. Offer 3-month retention incentives (free PT session, class pass top-up) to members in months 2–4 of membership — cheapest retention is early intervention.

• **Upsell PT & class packs now.** September hit £22k revenue on 168 members — your best month. That's driven by member growth, not pricing power. Introduce tiered class packages (4/8/12-class passes at 15–20% premium) and PT blocks (5 sessions at £75/hour). These convert idle capacity into margin without raising base membership.

• **Quiet class fill: track attendance by time slot in TeamUp.** If morning/midweek classes run <60% capacity, move one underused slot to a peak time (typically 6–7 pm) or trial a hybrid online option to fill it without new hire cost.
